boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UC Merced rituals and recurring celebrations, from the first walk across Scholars Bridge to service and alumni traditions.

cards.title: Begin the journey on Scholars Bridge
cards.subtitle: Annual new-student welcome tradition
cards.notes: If you are an incoming Bobcat, join the campus-led walk across Scholars Bridge and through the Beginnings Sculpture at the fall welcome.
cards.short_summary: UC Merced has marked new students’ academic beginnings with this bridge crossing since 2005.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced describes Scholars Bridge Crossing as an annual tradition since 2005 that commemorates the beginning of a student's academic journey.
cards.source_title: Scholars Bridge Crossing | Let the Journey Begin...
cards.access_notes: Event timing and participation details are announced by Student Affairs for each fall term.

cards.entity_name: Let the Journey Begin Journey Shirt
cards.title: Wear the incoming-class Journey Shirt
cards.subtitle: Scholars Bridge Crossing custom
cards.notes: At the fall crossing, look for the commemorative “Let the Journey Begin...” shirt distributed to incoming students as part of the ritual.
cards.short_summary: Matching Journey Shirts connect each incoming group to UC Merced’s earliest bridge-crossing ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs says students continue to receive a commemorative Journey Shirt as a nod to the white polos worn by the first class in 2005.
cards.source_title: Scholars Bridge Crossing | Let the Journey Begin...
cards.access_notes: Distribution is tied to the annual Scholars Bridge Crossing; consult the event announcement for eligibility.

cards.title: Gather beneath Beginnings for the class photo
cards.subtitle: Scholars Bridge Crossing photo tradition
cards.notes: When offered during Bridge Crossing, join the optional group photo in front of Beginnings to document the start of your UC Merced journey.
cards.short_summary: An optional aerial photo at Beginnings became a recognized component of the new-student crossing in 2016.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced Alumni states that the optional aerial photo in front of the Beginnings Sculpture was added to Scholars Bridge Crossing in 2016.
cards.access_notes: The photo is optional and may not be offered every year; rely on the current Bridge Crossing schedule.

cards.title: Make the return journey at commencement
cards.subtitle: Graduation procession tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, notice graduates being led through Beginnings in reverse, mirroring their arrival and marking their transition to alumni.
cards.short_summary: The crossing’s closing counterpart sends graduates back through the sculpture before commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Affairs says graduates in cap and gown are led through the Beginnings Sculpture in reverse before commencement to mark their transition from student to alum.
cards.source_title: Scholars Bridge Crossing | Let the Journey Begin...
cards.access_notes: This procession is part of university commencement programming; graduates should follow commencement instructions.

cards.title: Learn the campus alma mater, “My Merced”
cards.subtitle: UC Merced’s official alma mater
cards.notes: Listen for “My Merced” at ceremonial moments and follow the official recording or lyrics to recognize the song’s campus references.
cards.short_summary: Composer Jimmy Dunne wrote UC Merced’s official alma mater after researching the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced identifies “My Merced” as the campus's official alma mater and explains that it was commissioned for the university.
cards.access_notes: The official page includes audio and lyrics; ceremonial use varies by event.

cards.title: Spot the class-gift ceremonial mace
cards.subtitle: Commencement and academic-ceremony symbol
cards.notes: At a formal academic ceremony, look for the walnut ceremonial mace, a Class of 2008 gift that represents UC Merced’s history and ideals.
cards.short_summary: The locally crafted UC Merced Mace incorporates Central Valley walnut and ceremonial symbols.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced says its ceremonial mace was a gift from the Class of 2008 and was designed and created by local woodworker Pope Lawrence.
cards.access_notes: Observe it as part of university ceremonial pageantry; it is not a public hands-on object.

cards.title: Run or cheer at the Toloma 5K
cards.subtitle: Native American Heritage Month tradition
cards.notes: Check the fall calendar for this campus 5K, which recognizes Native American Heritage Month and follows a route through campus landmarks.
cards.short_summary: Since 2021, the Toloma 5K has paired a campus run with recognition of Yokut and Miwuk land.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced states that the Toloma 5K has been held since 2021; its name derives from the Miwuk word for bobcat.
cards.source_title: Toloma 5K Honors Native American Heritage at UC Merced
cards.access_notes: Registration, route, and participation details vary by year; use the current university event listing.

cards.title: Start the term with Welcome Back Week
cards.subtitle: Bobcat Spirit & Traditions program
cards.notes: Watch Student Involvement announcements at the start of term and choose a Welcome Back Week program that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: Welcome Back Week is one of the named traditions maintained through UC Merced’s Bobcat Spirit & Traditions work.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced’s Office of Student Involvement identifies Welcome Back Week, alongside Bridge Crossing, as an important campus tradition.
cards.source_title: Program Areas | Office of Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by term; check Student Involvement’s current calendar for activities and any registration.

cards.title: See the campus turn out for Bobcat Day
cards.subtitle: Annual open house for future Bobcats
cards.notes: If you are considering UC Merced, use the annual spring open house to take tours, attend sessions, and meet student groups.
cards.short_summary: Bobcat Day is UC Merced’s annual open house, bringing prospective students and families into campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced describes Bobcat Day as its annual open house for admitted students, their families, and friends.
cards.source_title: UC Merced to Welcome Future Bobcats at Bobcat Day Celebration
cards.access_notes: Held annually in spring; consult the current Bobcat Day page for registration and schedule information.

cards.entity_name: Bobcats Give Back: Day of Service
cards.title: Join Bobcats Give Back: Day of Service
cards.subtitle: Annual Student Philanthropy Month service tradition
cards.notes: Register when the annual service day is announced and contribute time alongside students, alumni, faculty, and staff on a community project.
cards.short_summary: This recurring service day turns Student Philanthropy Month into a shared community-maintenance effort.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Merced calls Bobcats Give Back: Day of Service an annual event during Student Philanthropy Month and lists students, alumni, faculty, and staff as invited volunteers.
cards.source_title: Student Philanthropy Month Returns to UC Merced with Focus on Service and Giving
cards.access_notes: The announced 2026 service day was March 14 at Lake Yosemite; future locations and sign-up details may change.
